title: Vanishing of the canonical Ext-two class characterizes lifting a bounded-above complex across a square-zero thickening

standard_prerequisites.use: Sites and sheaves of rings, bounded-above derived categories, flat resolutions, localization of the homotopy category, mapping cones and the four lemma. The canonical class and induced-map support are retained rather than assumed to give the lifting conclusion.

core_obligations: Retain the canonical obstruction construction and turn its vanishing in the derived category into a chain-level nullhomotopy after a quasi-isomorphic replacement.
Construct a lifted differential over the square-zero extension and use descending cohomological induction to show that reduction recovers the original bounded-above complex.

difficulty_reason: The difficult direction must produce an actual lifted complex from a derived nullhomotopy while preserving its reduction. The differential correction and comparison induction are concrete H2 deformation-theoretic work beyond an abstract obstruction-class citation.
